$comment: Flat list of valid/ fixture paths (relative to valid/, without extension) that are known to probe a numeric-domain boundary named in Sec 5 / Sec 8.1 / Sec 8.2. This file lives outside valid/ so a runner enumerating valid/**/*.json as fixtures never mistakes it for one (Sec 8.1, Sec 8.2). Listing a fixture here does NOT define what a wider-domain implementation's output must be -- it only tells the shared corpus runner that an implementation supporting a domain wider than the minimum (Sec 5) is exempt from matching this fixture's own <name>.json / <name>.canonical.ktav byte-for-byte. Such an implementation's correctness on these specific inputs is governed directly by Sec 5 (which numeric value and kind it holds) and Sec 5.9 (how it canonically writes whatever Value it actually holds), not by a pinned alternative oracle in this corpus. A minimum-domain-only implementation MUST match every fixture listed here exactly, the same as any other valid/ fixture -- for such an implementation these fixtures are in no way special.
